power: Implement shutdown after x. This codes sets an alarm for kShutdownAfterSecsPref on path to suspend (if one is not already running). On a wake up If in full resume : stops any running alarm. If in dark resume and not on line power: Forces a device shutdown instead of re-suspend if the alarm has already fired. If the alarm has not fired simply slips back to suspend. If in dark resume and on line power, simply slips back to suspend. Note that, a new alarm will be set again for kShutdownAfterSecsPref if one is not running. On a transition to full resume from dark resume Stops the running alarm. Note that this change does not handle shutting down the device if the battery is below a configured threshold. This is to follow in a seperate cl. Test cases are in the cl that this depends on. BUG=chromium:964510 TEST=deploy on device and make sure it works. Change-Id: Ic6ebafcb4bb044c7d0a4f46c82bd8b22a7694abe Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1627056 Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org>

In theory tests that requires a touchscreen should not be run on devices without one. This CL mitigates that issue by creating a virtual touchscreen (using the same API as the virtual keyboard). devices: block: issue fsync when FlushTimer expires The RequestType::Flush handler correctly uses fsync(), which issues an fsync to the underlying disk image file. However, the flush timer (started on write and cancelled if a flush request is executed) was only calling flush(), which is insufficient when the disk image is a raw file - it just flushes in-memory buffers and does not issue an fsync. CHROMIUM: add vmstat counts for different page fault types VM event counters are added to keep track of anonymous vs. file vs. shmem page faults. They are: pgmajfault_a, pgmajfault_f and pgmajfault_s. These are useful to analyze system performance, particularly when the cost of a fault for a file page is very different from that of an anonymous page, as would happen, for instance, in the presence of zram. The PGMAJFAULT counter is no longer directly maintained, for performance. Instead the three new counters are added whenever the total count is needed. This adds entries to /proc/vmstat. I considered adding them at the end for better compatibility, but the contents of /proc/vmstat are already highly variable depending on config options. It is still worth asking whether the new counters should NOT contain "pgmajfault" as a substring of their name. FROMLIST: Bluetooth: btusb: hci_event: handle msbc audio over USB Endpoints For msbc encoded audio stream over usb transport, btusb driver to be set to alternate settings 6 as per BT core spec 5.0. This done from hci_sync_conn_complete_evt. The type of air mode is known during this event. For this reason the btusb is to be notifed about the TRANSPARENT air mode and the ALT setting 6 is selected. The changes are made considering some discussion over the similar patch submitted earlier from Kuba Pawlak(link below) https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-bluetooth/msg64577.html (am from https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-bluetooth/msg76982.html) BUG=None TEST=Enable WBS in CRAS using cras_test_client --set_wbs_enabled 1. ichspi: Set EC region as RW if descriptor override is enabled If the flash descriptor override pin is asserted then the flash descriptor security is disabled. For most regions this is represented in the flash region status register, but since the EC does not have a defined bit in that register it looks at the descriptor directly and so it sees that the region is marked as read-only and treats it as such. In order to support flashing this region if descriptor override is enabled the code should first check for that state and mark the EC region as read-write if that is the case.
